text:
Priya (People Ops): Heads up 1: our candidate travel booking template got a question. We reimbursed overnight hotel for a candidate flying in, but they arrived a day early. The hiring team approved the extra night because of early arrival. Can we reimburse that extra night on the offer?

Liam (Recruiting): The hiring manager greenlit it verbally before offer acceptance. Candidate submitted receipts showing two nights; invoice shows two nights. They used a personal card.

Ava (Finance): For candidate travel we need explicit written pre-approval before reimbursement. If approval is only verbal, we need the hiring manager to send a short email confirming approval and the reason. Once we have that, finance can process the reimbursement.

Priya (People Ops): Does this require any change to the offer letter or the recruiter to note anything?

Liam (Recruiting): Not retroactively. For future hires, we should add a line in the booking template: "Any additional nights must be pre-approved in writing by the hiring manager." I'll add it to the template.

travel-bot: Policy note: Candidate travel reimbursables require documented pre-approval for any non-standard expenses (extra nights, upgraded class, companion travel). See internal candidate travel SOP. :memo:

Ava (Finance): Also, code this as "Candidate travel > Lodging - approved exception" and attach the manager email to the reimbursement ticket. If recruiter wants us to pay vendor (hotel) directly for future cases, finance can set up a PO if requested in advance.

Priya (People Ops): Okay I'll ask Liam to get that approval email, then we'll process. Also adding the booking template language now. Thanks!

Liam (Recruiting): Will do; I'll ping the hiring manager and get the confirmation.

Priya (People Ops): Closing loop in a day after I have the manager email.
